issues.legal_issue: Valuation of distillery assets and payment to an outgoing licensee are not prerequisites to transferring possession to an incoming licensee.
material_facts: The outgoing licensee’s term had expired, and a succeeding licensee had been granted the next term.
The outgoing licensee did not cooperate with requests to hand over the distillery or with efforts to assess the value of its assets.
The excise authorities took an inventory and transferred possession to the incoming licensee before the valuation was completed.
The licensing scheme regulated the continuing manufacture, storage, and supply of intoxicants, and the Court considered the need to avoid interruption and loss of public revenue.
issues.conclusion: Prior valuation and payment were neither mandatory nor a condition precedent to taking possession and handing the assets to the incoming licensee; the transfer of possession was not illegal.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 50 must be read as part of the licence’s integrated scheme, including clauses 2, 23(iii), 36(4), 39(1), 41, 42(1), and 44, and in light of the regulatory scheme under sections 13, 14, 17, and 62 of the Madhya Pradesh Excise Act, 1915. A practical construction that permits continuity of regulated supply is preferred to a strict construction that could cause disruption and loss of public revenue. Godhra Electricity Co. Ltd. v. State of Gujarat was distinguished because it concerned a statutory acquisition scheme and constitutional challenge in which the governing statute did not provide for subsequent interest. Har Shankar v. Deputy Excise and Taxation Commissioner and State of M.P. v. Nandlal Jaiswal were relied on for the State’s regulatory control over intoxicants and the absence of a fundamental right to trade in liquor.

predicates.regulated_license_transition_case: The proceeding concerns transfer of a regulated business from an outgoing licensee to a succeeding licensee.
predicates.outgoing_license_expired: The outgoing licensee’s term ended before the succeeding licensee took over.
predicates.outgoing_licensee_did_not_cooperate: The outgoing licensee did not cooperate with the handover or the assessment of the assets’ value.

issues.definition: When a regulated license transition follows expiry of the outgoing license and that licensee does not cooperate, the transfer may proceed without prior valuation and payment.

issues.legal_issue: An outgoing licensee is not entitled to restitution of transferred distillery assets when the succeeding licence has become final, the outgoing licence has expired, and prior valuation and payment are not conditions precedent to transfer.
material_facts: The succeeding license had become final and the outgoing license had expired.
The outgoing licensee had not cooperated with the handover.
The outgoing licensee had given up its challenge to the licence conditions in the High Court, and the valuation was not challenged in the writ petition.
The authorities had transferred the distillery assets and warehouses to the succeeding licensee.
issues.conclusion: The outgoing licensee was not entitled to restitution of the distillery plant, machinery, or attached warehouses.
issues.legal_principle: Because prior valuation and payment are not conditions precedent to transfer under the integrated licensing scheme, the transfer did not entitle the outgoing licensee to restitution. The Court also noted that the licence conditions had not been challenged and that the succeeding licence had become final. The Court distinguished Godhra Electricity Co. Ltd. v. State of Gujarat in the context of the different statutory scheme and constitutional challenge there.

rule.if: appeal_seeking_restitution_after_license_transfer and outgoing_license_expired and succeeding_license_final and transfer_not_illegal

predicates.appeal_seeking_restitution_after_license: The proceeding is an appeal seeking return of assets transferred from an outgoing licensee to a succeeding licensee.
predicates.outgoing_license_expired: The outgoing licensee’s term ended before the transfer.
predicates.succeeding_license_final: The succeeding license had become final.
predicates.transfer_not_illegal: The transfer was not unlawful because prior valuation and payment were not prerequisites to handover.

issues.definition: In an appeal seeking return of transferred assets, restitution is denied when the outgoing licence has expired, the succeeding licence is final, and the transfer was not unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: An outgoing licensee may seek an administrative determination of the value of transferred assets through a representation to the Government.
material_facts: The outgoing licensee disputed the value assigned to the assets but had not cooperated in the earlier valuation process.
The Court declined to decide the valuation dispute in the appeal.
The Court allowed the outgoing licensee to submit supporting material and directed that an appropriate senior Government officer consider the parties’ materials and provide a hearing if requested.
issues.conclusion: The outgoing licensee could make a representation to the Government, and an officer not below the rank of Secretary was to determine the value after considering the parties’ materials and giving a requested hearing.
issues.legal_principle: Although the Court did not determine the disputed valuation in the appeal, it permitted administrative reconsideration on a representation, with both sides able to submit material and an opportunity for a hearing through counsel if requested.

predicates.appeal_involving_disputed_asset_valuatio: The proceeding is an appeal involving a dispute about the value of assets transferred between licensees.
predicates.valuation_not_adjudicated_on_appeal: The appellate court does not itself decide the disputed valuation.
predicates.both_sides_can_submit_material: The outgoing and succeeding licensees can place material about the valuation before the Government.

issues.definition: When an appeal leaves an asset valuation dispute undecided and both sides can provide supporting material, an administrative valuation representation is permitted.
